title: WPMS/3180/2018 of M/S LINK ENTERPRISES Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 3180 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Deputy Advocate
General for the State of Uttarakhand.
The petitioner has entered into a contract
and executed a contract bond on 31.12.2016
being numbered as 29/SE-9/2014-15 dated
20.12.2014, and he has deposited a security for
the execution of the work under the contract to
the tune of `41,23,038/-. The work which the
petitioner was supposed to perform under the
contract was on the basis of the declaration,
which was made by the Hon'ble Chief Minister
of the State for construction of a steel bridge
from Raipur Kumlaada Kaddukhal to
Khairiman Singh.
The basic controversy which the
petitioner has tried to raise in the writ petition is
pertaining to the imposition of the GST at the
rate of 12% on the said contract.
He has submitted that as the contract
stood executed on 01.07.2017, i.e. even much
prior to the enforcement of the provisions of the
12% GST, to be included in the estimated cost,
he has submitted that raising his grievance
pertaining to the imposition of the GST and the
rate at which it would be levied he has already
represented his case before the respondent and
the same has not yet been considered and is
pending consideration.
During the course of argument, the
learned counsel for the petitioner has referred to
a judgment rendered by the Hon'ble High Court
adjudicature at Madras, wherein, he contends
that the identical controversy was taken into
consideration and adjudicated by the said Court
vide its judgment dated 05.10.2017.

His contention is that his case is also
covered by the aforesaid ratio, but he has
confined his writ petition for the grant of relief
to the effect that since as against the imposition
of 12% of the GST in addition to the value of
the work done by the petitioner under the
contract, he had already objected to the
imposition of the same by representing the
matter by submitting a representation on
05.10.2017 reiterating the same by submitting
yet another representation on 14.09.2018, but
the same has not yet been taken into
consideration and no decision has been taken as
to whether at all the petitioner would be liable
to pay 12% GST on the contract, which has
been executed prior to the enforcement of the
aforesaid amended provision.
At this stage this Court without
expressing any opinion on the merits of the
matter and considering the relief clause is
disposing of the writ petition directing the
competent authority as impleaded in the array
of the parties of the writ petition to take a
decision on the representation of the petitioner
as submitted on 05.10.2017 and 14.09.2018 and
pass an appropriate order after providing an
opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and also
taking into consideration the impact of the ratio
as propounded by the High Court of Judicature
at Madras. The decision on the representation is
directed to be taken within a period of two
months from the date of the production of the
certified copy of this order.
Subject to the above observation, the writ
petition stands disposed of.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 07.05.2019
Pooja
